lineas.texto: You wake up in a village in the year 1300. It's November, and the air smells of smoke.
The old English name for this month was the blood month. Here's why.
There isn't enough hay to feed every animal through the winter.
So around Saint Martin's day, the eleventh, many pigs and cattle are slaughtered.
Nothing is wasted. Meat is packed in salt, hung in the smoke, made into sausages.
Salt is expensive, so a family's salt barrel matters as much as the meat in it.
Tonight there's a rare feast of fresh meat, because tomorrow it all goes in the salt.
